clue.text: Publishing employee left page out, modern technology getting nothing right

indicators.note: the page is left out of the word for having departed, so its abbreviation is removed

parts.note: left, as in went away, means parted
IT, information technology, stands for modern computing
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A publishing worker walks out, leaving a page behind, while new tech gets nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes P from PARTED, leaving ARTED.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of illustrations at a publisher is a staff member of that business.

clue.text: Without love it's a strange upsetting liaison

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the letters go round the word for love
upsetting, in a down clue, turns the word for strange upside down

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: An odd, troubling affair conducted without any love at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns RUM into MUR, and 'Without' (meaning outside) puts it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret love affair, which the French borrowing names.

clue.text: Later, when darkness comes on, drunk hangs round

indicators.note: the word for drunk hangs around the little word on, enclosing it

parts.note: tight is informal for drunk
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk lingers about later on, once it gets dark.
explanation.definitionFit: The word refers to the coming evening or night of the current day, a later time after dusk.

clue.text: Lure of French, affectedly shy

parts.note: de is the French word for of
coy means pretending to be shy or modest

explanation.surface: A French temptress, putting on a show of shyness to draw someone in.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoy is something used to entice or trap, just as a lure is.

clue.text: Hawkish type in row with half the Scottish team

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: only half the team name is kept, its last three letters dropped

parts.note: Celtic is a Glasgow football club

explanation.surface: A warmonger quarrels with half of a Scottish football side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half the' trims CELTIC, a Glasgow football club, to CEL.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the term for a male falcon or hawk used in falconry, so literally a type of hawk.

clue.text: Tries somehow to hold tricky line, reluctant to cave in?

indicators.note: the first group holds the second inside it
somehow suggests the letters of tries arranged in some other way
tricky signals that the letters of line are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hold an awkward position, refusing to give in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' looks like the subject of the sentence and 'line' its object, but both are only fodder; each has its own scrambling word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tough and bouncing back means not giving way under pressure, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Religious book of knowledge, origin undiscovered

indicators.note: the start of the word is left uncovered, removing its first letter

parts.note: truth is what is known to be so

explanation.surface: A sacred text whose source is still unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a short book of the Old Testament, one of the scriptures.

clue.text: Sound of extra nonsense

definitions.meaning: the word film extras mutter to simulate background crowd chatter
also British slang for rubbish or empty talk

explanation.surface: A noise that adds nothing but more drivel.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage crowds famously murmur this vegetable's name as hubbub, and it is also slang for twaddle.

clue.text: Brutal ace found out, put in cell?

definitions.note: something placed within a cell structure

indicators.note: found out suggests the letters are taken out of order and recast

explanation.surface: A violent ace is caught and locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomically this is a small rod or bar dividing a cavity into cells, as in spongy bone tissue.

clue.text: Gosh! Cosy place is visible from coastal road

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
a niche is a snug recess or comfortable position

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a snug spot seen from the seaside drive.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a road cut along a cliff or coast, such as those on the Riviera.

clue.text: Cry from queen nipped by mammal

indicators.note: being nipped means being gripped, so the mammal surrounds the letter

parts.note: a seal is a marine mammal

explanation.surface: A monarch yelps after being bitten by an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A high shrill call or shriek is a kind of cry.

clue.text: Like amphibian in river, when it's very misty outside

indicators.note: the river's letter goes in the word for misty weather

parts.note: foggy describes thick misty weather

explanation.surface: A creature lurks in the river on a murky day.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means resembling a frog, the amphibian in question.

clue.text: Worried about English litres left in wine store

indicators.note: the word for worried goes about the three abbreviations

parts.note: to have cared is to have worried
L is the symbol for litres

explanation.surface: Someone frets over English litres abandoned in the wine cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine kept underground for ageing has been stored in a cellar, i.e. placed in a wine store.

clue.text: Spring fashion treated with contempt

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
ton is an old word for fashionable style

explanation.surface: This spring's clothing line is sneered at.
explanation.definitionFit: To expectorate on someone is to show utter scorn, so the phrase means scorned.

clue.text: Chum with a cord securing foot of awkwardish bird

indicators.note: the friend holds the letter fast inside

parts.note: a pal is a chum

indicators.note: in a down clue the foot is the bottom, i.e. last letter

parts.note: a rope is a cord

explanation.surface: A friend tethers a clumsy bird's foot with string.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small wading bird of the sandpiper family.

clue.text: One anxious when making digital contact

definitions.text: One anxious when making digital contact

parts.words: One anxious when making digital contact
parts.note: a nervous person puts fingers, the digits, to the teeth

explanation.surface: A worrier about getting in touch online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital contact' suggests computers, but digits are fingers, here meeting the teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitually nervous person chews their fingernails, so the term names a worrier.

clue.text: Before a fight have pork pie in lounge

indicators.note: before places the fib ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for lie
a bout is a fight

explanation.surface: Before a boxing match, eat a pork pie in the lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang a 'pork pie' (often 'porky') is a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf idly is to lounge, the verb meaning to laze.

clue.text: Snack with traditional jam providers brought into school

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: and means with or plus
the WI, Women's Institute, is famed for making jam

explanation.surface: A snack with homemade jam arrives at school.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI (Women's Institute) is a British women's organisation known for jam-making.
explanation.definitionFit: Filling between slices of bread makes a classic light meal or snack.

clue.text: Country retreat given visible sign

parts.note: a den is a private retreat
a mark is a visible sign or trace

explanation.surface: A rural hideaway is given a signpost.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Scandinavian nation, a country of northern Europe.

clue.text: New style identification has revolutionised biblical city

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turned round, so the city's name is reversed

parts.note: Gath was a Philistine city in the Bible, home of Goliath

explanation.surface: A trendy new label has turned an ancient city around.
explanation.definitionFit: A label preceded by the # symbol identifies a topic on social media, a modern form of tagging.

clue.text: Passage that is lined with rolled gold

indicators.note: the first word contains the second as a lining

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: rolled means turned over, so gold's heraldic name is reversed

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A corridor that is lined with gold leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold, a convention setters lean on often.
explanation.definitionFit: The gullet or windpipe is a passage in the neck.

clue.text: Survive defeat, admitting inadequate notion

indicators.note: the defeat lets the other piece in

parts.note: a rout is a heavy defeat

indicators.note: inadequate means lacking its final letter

parts.note: an idea is a notion

explanation.surface: One gets through a loss while confessing to a half-baked idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To weather a storm or crisis to its end is to come through it, i.e. survive.

clue.text: Interrupting major or minor stars, seize drug

indicators.note: the word for seize breaks into the constellation name

parts.note: Canis Major and Canis Minor are constellations
to nab is to seize

explanation.surface: Breaking into a starry scene, the police seize narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemp, smoked as marijuana, is an illegal recreational drug.

clue.text: Education expert's method in local authority

parts.note: a MEd is a Master of Education degree holder
a way is a method

explanation.surface: A teaching specialist's approach is adopted by the council.
explanation.walkthrough: Medway is a unitary authority (council area) in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: This Kent district is governed as a single council, a unitary local authority.

clue.text: Report of wee animal or a much bigger one

indicators.note: report suggests the spoken form, here a Scottish accent

parts.note: a mouse is a small creature, wee being the Scots word for small

explanation.surface: Rumour of a tiny creature or a huge one.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots, as in Burns's poem 'To a Mouse', mouse is pronounced 'moose'.
explanation.definitionFit: The elk of North America is a far larger beast than a mouse, so another animal.

clue.text: Glad to be spoilt when one's caught cold

indicators.note: the scrambled letters catch the numeral inside
spoilt means the letters of glad are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Happy to be pampered after catching a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be spoilt' turns GLAD into ALGD; 'caught' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare literary adjective meaning chilly or freezing.

clue.text: Musician from Australia in the marketplace

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the market

parts.note: a mart is a market
Oz is informal for Australia

explanation.surface: A performer from Down Under busking at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian composer is a famous musician.

clue.text: Rigorous to the end, letting nothing get in the way

indicators.note: the empty letter intrudes, getting inside the word

parts.note: through, as in read it through, means to the end
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Uncompromising to the finish, allowing no obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being complete and meticulous is being rigorous, a synonym.

clue.text: Impertinence that the head's on top of

definitions.meaning: cheek or brass, as in having the nerve

definitions.text: that the head's on top of
definitions.meaning: the part of the body supporting the head

explanation.surface: Cheek from someone the principal is lording it over.
explanation.definitionFit: It is slang for cheek or nerve and also the body part between head and shoulders.

clue.text: The definition of this sounds rude!

definitions.text: The definition of this sounds rude!

parts.words: The definition of this sounds rude!
parts.note: a synonym for the answer is rued, pronounced like rude

explanation.surface: A mock complaint that a dictionary entry is vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: The meaning, 'rued', is said just like 'rude'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rued means felt sorry about, and that word is spoken exactly like the word for impolite.
